title: A two-mode prediction test has low sensitivity to an imposed 30 ppm signal in KIC 10001893 residuals
abstract: We test whether two known stellar pulsations can predict the known 14.261 microHz signal in KIC 10001893. A fixed complex response uses the product of parent coefficients at 210.6816 and 196.4174 microHz. We fit the response in Kepler release 25 quarters 3 to 10 and test quarters 11 to 17. For 60-day windows, the response increases squared prediction error by 23 percent in aperture flux and 9 percent in corrected flux, relative to a steady signal. Quarter resampling gives wide intervals that include a gain. The weak parent has local coefficient errors near 45 to 50 ppm. In 500 residual tests with an imposed quadratic signal at a 30 ppm reference amplitude, measured parents give a positive gain in only 37 and 27 trials. True parent coefficients give a gain in 412 and 406 trials. Thus this test has low sensitivity under these noise and signal assumptions. The observed null result does not reject nonlinear pulsation or confirm a planet. The two flux products share exposures. Code, input hashes, local fits, aggregate results and external retrieval steps are included.

display.caption: Measured parent coefficients give positive gains in few imposed-signal trials. The same residuals with true parents give more gains. Each cell has 500 trials. This is a conditional simulation, not a planet recovery rate.

Local complex coefficients at the published parent difference. A response fitted in Q3 to Q10 predicts Q11 to Q17. Dotted lines divide the early and later window centers. The steady comparator uses the published slow frequency. Windows are cut at quarter edges.
